mods.t: Key Terms, Value and the Project Environment

p: A project is a temporary initiative in a unique context undertaken to create value. The unique context, not the unique output, is what makes it a project.

Several core definitions were updated for the first time in decades, and the exam tests the new wording. Project success is no longer scope, schedule and budget. It is the consensus view across intended beneficiaries, other stakeholders and participants that the project delivered value worth the effort and the expense.

Value is the excess of financial and non-financial benefits over the investment made. Different stakeholders perceive it differently, and all of those perceptions count toward the consensus judgement.

Projects sit inside a value delivery system — a collection of strategic business activities through which strategy becomes portfolios, programmes, projects, products and operations, and eventually realised benefit.

The project environment divides into factors you do not control and assets you own. Enterprise environmental factors are conditions outside the team's control, internal or external. Organizational process assets are the plans, processes, policies, procedures and knowledge bases the organization owns and can change.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: Value for the navy is delivered capability at sea; for the yard it is margin and capability retention; for the state it is ICV and skills transfer. Three different definitions, one consensus judgement.
Classification-society rules and export-control regulation are enterprise environmental factors. The yard cannot change them by decision.
The yard's own weld procedure library, its estimating database and its lessons learned from the previous class are organizational process assets.
The design licence agreement with the partner is an enterprise environmental factor for the project team, even though the yard signed it.
Learn the definition of a project verbatim. The unique context is the distinguishing element.
Test any constraint with one question: could the organization change it by decision? Yes means OPA; no means EEF.
Identify the value components for every stakeholder group, not only the paying customer.
Revisit the business case whenever the environment changes. Value is assessed continuously, not once.
Distinguish the project team from the project management team when reading role-based items.
On your own programme, which stakeholder's definition of value is least well understood by the delivery team?
Your notes

mods.t: The Six Principles and the Five Focus Areas

p: Principles guide behaviour and judgement; they are not prescriptive rules. That is precisely why the exam asks what you would do rather than what the rule says.

The eighth edition consolidates the seventh edition's twelve principles into six. Adopt a holistic view. Focus on value. Embed quality into processes and deliverables. Be an accountable leader. Integrate sustainability within all project areas. Build an empowered culture.

The five Focus Areas — Initiating, Planning, Executing, Monitoring and Controlling, Closing — return the familiar groupings but under a new name. The rename matters: today's projects satisfy these five concepts through formal processes, informal practices and flexible policies. Calling them Focus Areas removes the implication that a formal process must exist for each one.

Focus Areas are not phases and they are not sequential. In a predictive life cycle they appear roughly in order. In an adaptive life cycle, Planning, Executing and Monitoring recur inside every iteration.

Of the forty processes, two sit in Initiating, nineteen in Planning, eight in Executing, ten in Monitoring and Controlling and one in Closing. That distribution is itself informative: most project management work is planning.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: Holistic view: optimising block fabrication throughput while the erection berth is the constraint improves nothing. Measure the programme, not the shop.
Focus on value: if the follow-on hull option lapses, the business case for three-hull tooling changes materially. That is a value question, not a schedule question.
Embed quality: a weld fit-up gauge that only seats at a correct root gap prevents the defect; an extra NDT pass only finds it later and at higher cost.
Sustainability: blast media recovery, coating emissions, dock energy consumption and ICV workforce development are all FRIGATE BRAVO objectives with owners and metrics.
Empowered culture: the bay supervisor may draw contingency up to an agreed threshold. That threshold is what makes empowerment real rather than rhetorical.
Judge a decision against the principles when no process gives you an answer.
Attack the system, not the local symptom. Optimising a non-constraint gains nothing.
Give authority with a stated numerical threshold, never without limit.
Treat sustainability as a project area with metrics and owners, not as a policy statement.
Do not assume Focus Areas run in sequence. In adaptive work they recur every iteration.
Which of the six principles is weakest in your own organization, and what would be the first visible sign if it improved?
Your notes
2 processes        19 processes        8 processes        10 processes        1 process
The development approach is a spectrum, not three boxes. Tailoring is expected of every project; it reduces ceremony and effort, never accountability.

Approximately 40% of exam items reflect predictive approaches and the remaining 60% is divided between adaptive and hybrid. Approaches are not isolated to any one domain or task — they appear throughout all three ECO domains.

What pushes a scope area toward predictive: stable and well-understood requirements, heavy regulatory or certification approval, a high cost of change, and contractually fixed scope. What pushes it toward adaptive: emergent or contested requirements, rapid feedback, a low cost of change, and value that can be delivered incrementally.

Tailoring is the deliberate adjustment of approach, governance and processes to fit the context. The four steps are: select an initial development approach, tailor for the organization, tailor for the project, then implement ongoing improvement.
What you may never tailor away: governance obligations, regulatory compliance and ethical duties. You tailor how you meet them, never whether you meet them.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: Hull structure is predictive: the design is licensed and frozen, class approval gates every stage, and the cost of change after block closure is severe.
Combat-system integration is adaptive: requirements are emergent, the customer can give feedback on each increment, and software change is comparatively cheap.
Outfitting is hybrid: routing is predictive and drawing-driven, while compartment fit-out is refined with the end users.
The seam sits at physical installation. The adaptive stream must deliver a stable increment at each predictive milestone — those dates are fixed even though the content flexes.
Governance cannot be tailored lighter on FRIGATE BRAVO: the contract, the class regime and export controls all demand auditability.
Choose the approach per scope area, not per project.
Name every seam between approaches, give it a date and give it an owner.
Tailor ceremony and artifact count; never tailor away a governance or regulatory obligation.
State two factors behind every approach decision, so the decision can be revisited when they change.
Where a physical installation date is fixed, flex the content of an increment, not the date.
In your own programme, is there a scope area currently being run predictively that would be better run adaptively — and what prevents the change?
Your notes
Governance answers three questions: who may decide what, at which threshold does a decision escalate, and how do we know the project is still worth doing?
Governance carries nine of the forty processes and frames all the others. It authorises the project, integrates the plans, controls change and closes the work.

In Initiating: Initiate Project or Phase. In Planning: Integrate and Align Project Plans, and Plan Sourcing Strategy. In Executing: Manage Project Execution, Manage Quality Assurance, and Manage Project Knowledge. In Monitoring and Controlling: Monitor and Control Project Performance, and Assess and Implement Changes. In Closing: Close Project or Phase.
The charter authorises the project and names the project manager with a defined authority level. It is issued and signed by the sponsor, never by the project manager.

Governance models range from structured — a defined board with defined decision rights and reporting cadence — to self-governed, where the team holds decision rights within agreed boundaries. Culture determines which will actually work.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: A three-tier structure: the project manager decides within a 5% contingency draw; the programme board decides above it; the customer decides anything touching contracted scope or the certification basis.
The charter fixes the 46-month objective to SAT and names the propulsion package as a known constraint from month 9.
Success criteria include ICV content achieved and class certification obtained without conditional release — not only date and cost.
Manage Project Knowledge matters disproportionately here: first-of-class lessons are the largest cost lever on the two follow-on hulls.
Write the authority level as a number, not as an adjective.
Define escalation thresholds before they are needed, not when a variance appears.
Agree success metrics at initiation, or success becomes an argument at closure.
Match the governance model to the culture. A structured board imposed on a self-governed culture is theatre.
Capture lessons continuously; do not defer knowledge management to closure.
On your own programme, can every team leader state the threshold at which their decision leaves their hands?
Your notes
Assess the impact, route it for decision, then implement and update the baselines and the documents. The sequence never changes, whoever is asking.

Any stakeholder may request a change. The request is logged, its impact on scope, schedule, cost, risk and quality is assessed, a recommendation is made, and an authorised body decides. Only then is the change implemented, the baselines updated and the decision communicated.
Corrective action addresses performance that has already deviated. Preventive action addresses performance expected to deviate. Both are change requests, and both go through the same route.
A defect repair corrects a non-conforming deliverable. It is also a change request.

The most common wrong answer in change-control items is to implement the change to keep the customer happy. The correct first move is almost always to assess the impact and take it through the process — even when the sponsor asks personally, and even when the change looks small.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: A class surveyor requiring an additional bulkhead penetration seal after block closure is a change request — not a defect and not an emergency.
A partner-requested design refinement that the yard absorbs without logging is scope creep, however cooperative it feels at the time.
The programme director asking informally for a secondary damage-control console is still a change request. Sponsor authority does not bypass the process.
On the adaptive combat-system stream, a scope change is absorbed by reordering the backlog rather than by raising a change request — but only for scope that sits inside that stream.
Assess impact before you recommend, and recommend before anyone decides.
Route every change through the process, however small and whoever asks.
Update the baselines and the affected documents after approval, not before.
Communicate the status of proposed changes, not only approved ones.
Never re-baseline outside approved change control.
On your own programme, how many changes in the last quarter were implemented before they were assessed?
Your notes
The stakeholder register is not the deliverable. What you manage is the gap between where each stakeholder is and where the project needs them to be.

Seven processes sit in this domain. Identify Stakeholders in Initiating; Plan Stakeholder Engagement and Plan Communications Management in Planning; Manage Stakeholder Engagement and Manage Communications in Executing; Monitor Stakeholder Engagement and Monitor Communications in Monitoring and Controlling.
Identification is an Initiating process that repeats throughout. New stakeholders appear as the project moves through phases, and the register is a living artifact.

Engagement levels run unaware, resistant, neutral, supportive and leading. The engagement plan records the current and the desired level for each stakeholder, and the strategy is the route between them.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: Six stakeholder groups across four organizations. The naval customer and the design partner are high power and high interest and are managed closely. The class society is high power and medium interest and is kept satisfied — which on this programme means never surprised.
Yard trade unions began resistant on the shift pattern and moved to neutral after early consultation on the ICV plan. That movement is what Monitor Stakeholder Engagement exists to record.
The customer's resident engineer is on site daily and is a different stakeholder from the customer's programme office, with different information needs.
The local community is low power and medium interest — monitored through environmental and noise reporting, not engaged intensively.
Re-run stakeholder identification at every phase boundary, not only at kickoff.
Record current and desired engagement, and manage the gap.
Engage a resistant stakeholder to understand the cause before adjusting their involvement.
Treat the resident engineer and the programme office as separate stakeholders with separate needs.
Monitor satisfaction between formal acceptance events, so surprises surface early.
On your own programme, which stakeholder has moved from supportive to neutral in the last six months without anyone recording it?
Your notes
Push communication confirms that information was sent. It never confirms that it was understood.
Communication channels grow as n(n−1)/2 where n is the number of people. Adding one person to a ten-person team adds ten channels, not one.

Three modes. Interactive is real-time exchange — meetings, calls, stand-ups; highest bandwidth and highest cost. Push is sent to specific recipients — reports, emails, memos. Pull is accessed at will — dashboards, repositories, information radiators.
The barriers the exam expects you to name: noise, language and cultural difference, unstated assumptions, and distance or time zones, which push teams away from interactive modes.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: One reporting spine feeds three audiences at different depths: the yard team daily, the programme board monthly, and the naval customer at milestones.
Class hold-point notifications go out at a fixed lead time agreed with the surveyor. Missing that lead time is a compliance issue, not a courtesy issue.
Partner engineering-change bulletins are issued per increment and require acknowledgement, because a missed revision reaches the yard as an installed error.
The core team is 14 people, which is 91 channels. Adding the partner and customer representatives takes it to 20 people and 190 channels — which is why the plan exists.
State what, to whom, in what format, how often and by which method for every information flow.
Establish a feedback loop for anything that must be acted on, not only received.
Move to an interactive mode when a stakeholder has not acted on pushed information.
Recalculate channels when the team grows; the plan that worked at ten people will not work at twenty.
Agree notification lead times with external parties in writing.
On your own programme, which weekly report would nobody notice if it stopped being issued?
Your notes
Resources covers people and physical resources together, because on a real programme they are optimised together — crews, cranes, dock time and materials.
Five processes. Plan Resource Management and Estimate Resources in Planning; Acquire Resources and Lead the Team in Executing; Monitor and Control Resourcing in Monitoring and Controlling.

Resource levelling adjusts the schedule to fit resource limits and can extend the critical path. Resource smoothing works only within existing float and never moves the finish date. The exam tests this distinction repeatedly.
A responsibility assignment matrix carries exactly one accountable party per activity. Two accountable parties in one row is a defect, and so is none.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: The binding constraint at peak erection is certified welder capacity by process and position — a competence constraint, not a headcount one.
Heavy-lift crane hours and dry-dock occupancy compete with two other yard programmes. Acquiring them is a negotiation, not a booking.
Class surveyor availability for 61 hold points is a physical resource the yard does not control at all.
Partner secondees support technology transfer against the ICV target, which makes them simultaneously a resource and a compliance obligation.
Track competence, not only headcount, wherever certification gates the work.
Check every RACI row for exactly one accountable party.
Negotiate with functional managers before escalating a resource conflict to the sponsor.
Use smoothing when the finish date must hold; use levelling when the resource limit is absolute.
Treat resources the project does not control — surveyors, shared docks — as constraints, not as bookings.
On your own programme, which resource is genuinely constrained by certification rather than by headcount?
Your notes

mods.t: Leading the Team, Conflict and Knowledge

p: Leadership is a behaviour available to anyone on the team, not a position on the chart. Conflict is normal; what matters is which mode you reach for first.

The five conflict modes in PMI's order of preference: collaborate or problem-solve, which produces a durable solution and is the preferred answer whenever time permits; compromise or reconcile; smooth or accommodate, which buys time without resolving; force or direct, appropriate only in a genuine emergency; and withdraw or avoid, legitimate only for trivial issues or when tempers need to cool.
Team development runs forming, storming, norming, performing and adjourning. Storming is expected, not a failure of leadership. A team re-formed with new members returns to forming.

Knowledge is tacit and explicit. Tacit knowledge transfers through interaction — pairing, shadowing, communities of practice. Explicit knowledge transfers through documents. A repository alone is not knowledge management.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: One team across three organizational cultures: yard trades, partner secondees and customer representatives. Three sets of norms, one team charter.
The partner secondee programme is simultaneously a knowledge-transfer mechanism and an ICV obligation with contractual consequence.
First-of-class tacit knowledge — how a particular block sequence actually goes together — is the single largest cost lever on the follow-on hulls, and it does not live in any document.

A dispute between the yard's welding engineer and the partner's design authority over an accepted deviation is a conflict with contractual consequences, and collaboration is the only mode that resolves it.
Collaborate first whenever time permits.
Revisit the team charter whenever the team composition changes materially.
Match leadership style to the situation and the team's maturity, not to your own preference.
Transfer tacit knowledge through interaction; documents alone will not carry it.
Capture lessons continuously, and make them accessible — an artifact nobody can find has no value.
On your own programme, what tacit knowledge would be lost tomorrow if one specific person left?
Your notes
Best  →  sometimes  →  temporary  →  last resort  →  rarely
Control Quality checks correctness against specification and produces verified deliverables. Validate Scope obtains formal acceptance and produces accepted deliverables. Quality always comes first.

Six processes. Plan Scope Management, Elicit and Analyze Requirements, Define Scope and Develop Scope Structure in Planning; Monitor and Control Scope and Validate Scope in Monitoring and Controlling.

Requirements elicitation sits inside this domain in the eighth edition; it is not a separate knowledge area. The requirements traceability matrix links each requirement to its source and to the deliverable that satisfies it, and it is how scope creep is detected.

Scope creep is uncontrolled expansion without adjusting time, cost or resources — usually externally driven. Gold plating is the team adding features nobody requested — internally driven. Both are failures, and both are wrong answers when offered as a course of action.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: Operational requirements come from the navy, regulatory requirements from the class society, and interface requirements from the design partner. Three sources, one traceability matrix.
The scope statement states explicitly that in-service support and crew training are excluded. Exclusions prevent the expensive assumption that surfaces at handover.

Block acceptance runs quality first: the class surveyor releases the hold point, then the customer's resident engineer accepts the block. Reversing that order would present unverified work for acceptance.
Hull scope is baselined and change-controlled. Combat-system scope is deliberately left refinable so that operational feedback can reach it before installation closes access.
Write exclusions as carefully as inclusions.
Maintain the traceability matrix; it is how creep becomes visible.
Run Control Quality before Validate Scope, always.
Route every scope request through change control, however cooperative it feels.
Deliver to the requirement. Propose improvements as changes, not as gifts.
On your own programme, could you produce a traceability matrix today — and would it reconcile?
Your notes
The 100% rule: the work breakdown structure contains all of the scope and nothing outside it. The lowest level is the work package — estimable, assignable and controllable.
A work breakdown structure decomposes deliverables, not activities. Activities come later, in scheduling. Each element carries a code of accounts identifier so cost and progress roll up.
The WBS dictionary carries the detail behind each element: description, acceptance criteria, assumptions and responsible party.
On adaptive scope the equivalent structure is a product backlog, ordered by value and refined continuously so that the top of it is always ready to pull into the next iteration.
The scope baseline is the scope statement, the WBS and the WBS dictionary together — not the WBS alone.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: Five level-1 elements: hull structure, propulsion and auxiliary machinery, combat system, outfitting, and test and trials. Three different development approaches inside one structure.
The hull branch decomposes to work-package level: blocks 01–08, then cut and form, sub-assembly, block assembly, pre-outfit and class release.
The combat-system branch is not decomposed into a WBS at all. It is a nine-increment backlog with staged acceptance per increment.
Both roll up into one scope baseline and one budget, which is what makes it one programme rather than two.
Apply the 100% rule at every level, including for work that is not a physical deliverable.
Decompose deliverables, not activities.
Give every element a code of accounts identifier.
Write acceptance criteria into the WBS dictionary, not only into the contract.
Use a backlog where scope is emergent; do not force it into a WBS to look consistent.
On your own programme, is inspection and approval work represented in the breakdown — or assumed?
Your notes
Every estimate carries a basis: the assumptions, the constraints and the confidence behind the number. The basis of estimates is an examinable artifact in its own right.

Analogous estimating is top-down from a similar past project, adjusted for known differences — fast and least accurate. Parametric estimating applies a statistical rate to a quantity — accurate when the historical data is good. Bottom-up estimates every work package and rolls up — most accurate and most effort. Multipoint or three-point estimating expresses uncertainty as a range.
The beta or PERT formula is (O + 4M + P) / 6. The triangular formula is (O + M + P) / 3. Standard deviation is (P − O) / 6. If an item does not name the distribution, use beta.
Resource estimating and duration estimating are different questions. More resources may reduce duration, but not on activities that cannot be split.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: Hull steel is estimated parametrically: welder-hours per metre of weld by position and process, derived from the previous class of vessel.
Combat-system integration is estimated bottom-up by increment, because no comparable exists.
Long-lead equipment is not estimated at all — it comes from vendor quotation, which is a different kind of number with a different confidence.
The class hold-point work is estimated three-point, because surveyor availability introduces genuine uncertainty that a single-point number would conceal.
Record the basis of estimates for every number you produce.
Use beta unless the item names a different distribution.
Divide the standard deviation by six, never by four.
Use three-point estimating wherever uncertainty is material, and report the range.
Do not confuse resource estimating with duration estimating.
On your own programme, which estimate would you be least comfortable defending to the board — and what is its basis?
Your notes

mods.t: The Schedule Domain, Network Analysis and Compression

p: The critical path is the longest path through the network and it determines the shortest possible project duration. Activities on it have zero total float.
Three processes only: Plan Schedule Management and Develop Schedule in Planning, and Monitor and Control Schedule in Monitoring and Controlling. They carry all the network analysis.
Total float is LS − ES, which equals LF − EF. Free float is the delay available without delaying any successor. Negative float means the schedule is already behind a constraint.

Crashing adds resources to critical activities: it increases cost and does not work on every activity. Fast tracking runs sequential activities in parallel: it adds rework risk rather than cost. Neither changes scope — reducing scope is a change request.

The four dependency types are mandatory, discretionary, external and internal. Only discretionary dependencies can be renegotiated freely. Leads accelerate a successor and lags delay one; neither changes the activity's own duration.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: The erection sequence is constrained by crane availability, a shared dock window and 61 class hold points.
Coating cure time is a lag, not an activity. It consumes calendar time but no resource, and modelling it as an activity with effort overstates the resource plan.

The propulsion package is on the critical path from month 9. No amount of crashing hull fabrication recovers a late engine — which is why procurement lead time is a schedule input, not a procurement detail.
Fast tracking erection and outfitting is available but adds rework risk in compartments where access closes after block closure.
Compute the forward and backward passes before you decide anything.
Confirm which path is critical before spending money to compress.
Use fast tracking when cost is the binding constraint and rework is tolerable.
Use crashing when rework is unacceptable, for example on class-witnessed work.
Never re-baseline outside approved change control.
On your own programme, does anyone recalculate the critical path after each major milestone — or is it the one drawn at the start?
Your notes
Adaptive work is scheduled, not unscheduled. The instruments differ from a network diagram, but the purpose — forecasting rather than reporting — is identical.

Agile release planning sets the horizon: which increments make up the next release and roughly when. Iteration planning sets the commitment for the next iteration. Backlog refinement is continuous, keeping the top of the backlog ready to pull.

Velocity is points completed per iteration, observed rather than assigned. It is used to forecast a range, never to promise a date, and it is never compared between teams because story points are relative to one team's own baseline.

A burndown chart shows work remaining against time; it is simple but hides scope change. A burnup chart shows work completed against a scope line and therefore reveals scope growth. A cumulative flow diagram shows work in each state over time and exposes bottlenecks and work-in-progress build-up.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: The combat-system stream runs nine increments with staged acceptance. Release planning fixes which increments must be complete before each predictive integration milestone.
Velocity across the first four increments gives a forecast range for the remaining five — which is what the programme board needs, not a single promised date.
A burnup chart is used deliberately rather than a burndown, because the customer has added scope twice and a burndown would have concealed it.
The integration dates are fixed by hull access closing. When an increment cannot be completed, the content flexes and the date holds.
Forecast a range from observed velocity; never promise a single date from it.
Never compare velocity between teams.
Use a burnup chart wherever scope may change.
Refine the backlog continuously so the top is always ready.
Where a physical integration date is fixed, flex content and hold the date.
On your own programme, is any adaptive work being reported with a burndown chart while its scope is still moving?
Your notes
Cost baseline equals work package estimates plus contingency reserve. Project budget equals cost baseline plus management reserve. Drawing management reserve changes the baseline and needs approval.
The eighth edition names this domain Finance rather than Cost, because it covers funding strategy, funding proposals, revenue forecasts and financial governance — not only estimates.
Four processes: Plan Financial Management, Estimate Costs and Develop Budget in Planning; Monitor and Control Finances in Monitoring and Controlling.

Contingency reserve is held for identified risks that have a planned response. It sits inside the cost baseline and the project manager may draw it within an agreed threshold. Management reserve is held for unknown-unknowns, sits outside the baseline but inside the budget, and requires sponsor approval.
Funding limit reconciliation matters where the customer's payment milestones do not match the spend profile — which is normal on shipbuilding contracts and creates a working-capital constraint.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: Foreign-exchange exposure on the propulsion and sensor packages is a financial planning matter set in the financial management plan, not a procurement afterthought.
The customer pays at milestones; the yard spends continuously. The gap between the two is a funding requirement, and it is reconciled at budget development, not discovered later.
Contingency on FRIGATE BRAVO is sized from the risk register by expected monetary value, not as a flat percentage of the budget.
Combat-system increments are measured on accepted functionality rather than on hours burned, because hours burned on rejected work is not earned value.
Size contingency from the risk register, not as a percentage.
Keep management reserve outside the baseline and require sponsor approval to draw it.
Reconcile the spend profile against the funding profile at budget development.
Measure adaptive work on accepted functionality, not on hours consumed.
Set the foreign-exchange basis in the financial management plan, before the first purchase order.
On your own programme, is contingency derived from the risk register — or from habit?
Your notes
Every variance is earned value minus something. Every index is earned value divided by something. Negative or below 1.0 is always bad.
Schedule variance is EV − PV and cost variance is EV − AC, both expressed in currency. Schedule performance index is EV / PV and cost performance index is EV / AC, both ratios.

Estimate at completion has two common forms. Where the current variance is typical and will continue, EAC equals BAC divided by CPI. Where the variance was a one-off, EAC equals AC plus (BAC − EV). Read the item for which applies before choosing.
Estimate to complete is EAC minus AC. Variance at completion is BAC minus EAC. To-complete performance index is (BAC − EV) divided by (BAC − AC) — the efficiency needed to finish on budget.
Controlling finance is not reporting what was spent. The examinable output is a forecast with a stated basis.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: Hull and outfitting are measured by earned value against the performance measurement baseline.
Combat-system increments are measured by accepted increment, because partially integrated software has no meaningful percentage complete.
The single integrated report to the programme board reconciles both, plus long-lead expediting status against need dates.
At month 18 the programme is behind and over: SPI 0.92 and CPI 0.89, with a forecast overrun of $75.4m.
Write the nine formulas on scratch paper before reading the first question.
Determine whether the variance is typical before choosing an EAC formula.
Report variance at completion to the board, not only period variances.
Use to-complete performance index to test whether a recovery plan is arithmetically possible.
Measure adaptive work on accepted increments, not on effort consumed.
On your own programme, does the board receive a forecast at completion — or a spend-to-date report?
Your notes
Assurance audits the process; control inspects the deliverable. Low grade can be perfectly acceptable; low quality never is.

Manage Quality Assurance sits in the Governance domain and audits whether the quality processes are being followed and are capable. Control Quality inspects specific deliverables and produces verified deliverables, which then go to Validate Scope for acceptance.

Cost of quality has four categories. Prevention — training, qualified procedures, error-proofing — is cheapest. Appraisal is inspection and testing. Internal failure is rework found before handover. External failure is defects found in service, and is by far the most expensive.

Quality means conformance to requirements at whatever grade was specified. Grade is the category of features. A low-grade product that conforms is acceptable; a high-grade product that does not conform is not.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: Weld procedure qualification, the NDT sampling regime and coating inspection all sit inside the class survey framework, which is an external requirement rather than a yard choice.
A fit-up gauge that only seats at a correct root gap is prevention. An additional NDT pass is appraisal. The gauge is cheaper and works earlier.
External failure on a warship means a defect found at HAT, SAT or in service, when the compartment is complete and the programme is on the critical path. The multiplier is severe.
Sustainability sits inside this task in the ECO alongside cost of quality — coating emissions and blast media recovery are quality-plan content, not a separate policy.
Build quality in through prevention; do not rely on finding defects reliably.
Run Control Quality before Validate Scope.
Distinguish grade from quality when reading any requirement item.
Treat regulatory and class requirements as quality requirements, not as paperwork.
Disclose a compliance lapse immediately; concealment converts a mistake into misconduct.
On your own programme, what proportion of the quality budget is prevention rather than appraisal?
Your notes
Cheapest  →  most expensive
Match the contract to the certainty of the scope, not to the buyer's preference. Fixed price on undefined scope transfers risk to a claim, not to the seller.

Fixed-price contracts place cost risk on the seller and require well-defined scope. Cost-reimbursable contracts place cost risk on the buyer and suit emergent scope. Time and materials is a hybrid used for short engagements and staff augmentation.

Incentive-fee variants share the risk: fixed price incentive fee and cost plus incentive fee both link the fee to performance against a target. Fixed price with economic price adjustment protects both parties on multi-year contracts with commodity or currency exposure.
Make-or-buy analysis is not a pure cost decision. Capability retention, localization obligations and strategic risk all belong in it.
Source selection criteria are weighted and agreed before bids are opened. Adjusting them after opening bids is a governance failure whatever the commercial logic.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: Hull scope is firm fixed price: the design is licensed and frozen and the quantities are known.
Combat-system integration services are cost plus incentive fee, because the scope is refined increment by increment and no seller could price it firmly.
The propulsion package has a single credible source through the design partner, which removes competitive leverage and makes the negotiation strategy the main protection.
Hull steel is ICV-eligible and is deliberately sourced to develop a local mill, which is a strategic decision that a pure cost comparison would reverse.
Match the contract type to scope certainty.
Agree and weight source selection criteria before bids are opened.
Include capability retention and localization obligations in make-or-buy analysis.
Determine the negotiation strategy before entering the negotiation, especially with a sole source.

Your notes
A risk is a future uncertain event. Once it has occurred it is an issue and moves to the issue log. Half the response strategies tested are about opportunities.
Six processes. Plan Risk Management, Identify Risks, Perform Risk Analysis and Plan Risk Responses in Planning; Implement Risk Responses in Executing; Monitor Risks in Monitoring and Controlling.

Threat strategies are avoid, transfer, mitigate, accept and escalate. Opportunity strategies mirror them: exploit, share, enhance, accept and escalate. Accept is the only strategy identical on both sides, and escalate is the only one that leaves the project.
Expected monetary value is probability multiplied by impact. Threats carry negative impact and opportunities positive, so a total nets them rather than adding absolute values.
Implement Risk Responses is the process most often skipped in practice, and the exam knows it. A register full of planned responses that were never funded or scheduled is a finding.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: The carried FRIGATE BRAVO register: propulsion delivered late (40%, −$4.0m); class surveyor unavailable (30%, −$0.9m); combat-system requirements churn (55%, −$2.2m); certified welder shortage (35%, −$1.2m); and the follow-on hull option exercised early (25%, +$6.0m).
Net expected monetary value is approximately −$2.0m, which is what contingency is sized against.
Escalate is used for the export-control exposure, because it sits above the project's authority and belongs to the organization.
Reserve analysis each month compares remaining contingency against remaining risk. Contingency depleting faster than risk is retiring is the early-warning signal.
Force at least three opportunities into every risk register.
Give every response an owner and a trigger condition.
Fund and schedule risk responses; a register entry is not an implementation.
Net threats against opportunities when totalling expected monetary value.
Run reserve analysis monthly and act on the trend, not the balance.
On your own programme, how many opportunities are in the risk register — and when were they last reviewed?
Your notes
On a defence newbuild, compliance is scope. It drives real cost and real schedule, and a breach can stop the programme.

The ECO asks you to confirm compliance requirements, classify compliance categories, determine potential threats to compliance, use methods to support compliance, analyse the consequences of non-compliance, determine the necessary actions, and measure the extent to which the project is in compliance. Measurement is a named enabler — compliance that is asserted but not measured fails the task.

A risk is a future uncertain event; once it occurs it is an issue and moves to the issue log. An impediment or blocker is anything stopping the team progressing right now: evaluate the impact, prioritise, intervene, and reassess continually because removing one blocker often exposes the next.
Escalate only what the team genuinely cannot resolve, and escalate with a recommendation rather than a complaint.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: Four compliance regimes run simultaneously: classification-society rules, export control on the sensor suite, health and safety regulation governing confined-space and hot work, and the ICV commitment with contractual consequence if missed.
A blocked class inspection slot stops three blocks at once. That is an impediment with a same-day impact assessment, not a risk to monitor.
An export-control rule change would be simultaneously an external environment change, a compliance issue, a procurement risk and a backlog reprioritisation — one event reaching four registers.
The welder qualification lapse is a compliance breach with legal exposure, not a quality observation.
Classify every compliance requirement and define how compliance will be measured.
Move a materialised risk to the issue log the day it occurs.
Evaluate impediment impact before prioritising, and reassess after each removal.
Escalate with a recommendation and a decision date.
Analyse the consequence of non-compliance in advance, not after a breach.
On your own programme, how is compliance measured — or is it only asserted at audit?
Your notes
AI recommends; the project manager decides and remains accountable for the decision. Sustainability is one of the six principles, not an appendix to the plan.

Sustainability is environmental, social and economic — not environmental alone. In the ECO it appears inside critical information requirements, cost of quality, compliance and risk response. If it is a project objective it needs a metric, a baseline and a report like any other objective.

Appendix X3 of the eighth edition covers artificial intelligence in the project context: analysing data for insight, predicting risk, automating routine reporting and supporting forecasting. Its impact depends on the quality of the inputs and on human oversight, and PMI is explicit that ethical concerns and responsible use are part of the topic.

Organizational change runs both ways. Projects change organizations, and organizations change under projects. A restructure, a merger or a leadership change alters sponsorship, priorities and resource access — reassess the project rather than continuing on the old assumptions.
External environment change — regulation, technology, geopolitics, market — should reach the scope or the backlog, not only the risk register.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: Sustainability objectives on FRIGATE BRAVO: blast media recovery rate, coating emissions against consent limits, dock energy consumption, and local workforce development under ICV. Each has an owner and a metric.
AI is used to analyse the historical estimating database and to flag long-lead items trending toward their need dates. It does not approve a purchase order.

A yard restructure at month 22 changes the sponsor. The correct response is to reassess sponsorship, priorities and resource access — not to continue and hope the new sponsor inherits the commitments.

If the customer signals the follow-on hull option may lapse, that reaches the business case, not merely the risk register. The $8m of three-hull tooling and the ICV supplier programme both assumed three hulls.
Give every sustainability objective a metric, a baseline and an owner.
Keep a human accountable for every AI-supported decision.
Reassess sponsorship and priorities after any organizational change.
Let external change reach the scope or backlog, not only the risk register.
Escalate a business-case change with options, not with a problem statement.
On your own programme, which sustainability objective has an owner but no metric?

Closure is a process, not an event. A cancelled project is still closed formally, with lessons learned, procurement closure and resource release.
Work performance data is raw measurement. It becomes work performance information after analysis and work performance reports after packaging for an audience. Items test that chain.

Artifacts must be created, reviewed, updated and kept accessible. Accessibility is a named ECO enabler — an artifact nobody can find has no value. Tailor which artifacts you need; producing all of them is over-processing.

Closure covers obtaining stakeholder approval of completion, determining the criteria for closing, validating readiness for transition to operations or the next phase, and concluding activities including final lessons learned, retrospectives, procurement closure, financial closure and resource release.
Transition readiness is examinable. Handing over to an operations team that is not ready to receive is a closure failure even when the deliverable is complete.

s.he: Naval shipbuilding application — Project FRIGATE BRAVO
p: Closure includes handover to the in-service support organization, and closing both the partner licence and every equipment contract.
Phase closure is distinct from project closure: each block has closure criteria at class release, and each combat-system increment at staged acceptance.
Lessons from the lead frigate must reach the yard's organizational process assets before the follow-on hulls are authorised, or they are lost.
If FRIGATE BRAVO were cancelled at month 20, the closure obligations would remain: lessons learned, procurement closure, financial closure and resource release all still apply.
Tailor which artifacts you produce; do not produce all of them by default.
Make artifacts accessible to those who need them, not merely existent.
Capture lessons throughout, and push them into the organizational process assets at closure.
Validate that the receiving organization is ready before handing over.
Close a cancelled project formally; the obligations do not disappear.

mods.t: Your Study Plan and the Application

p: The most useful output of the mock is not the score. It is the classification of your wrong answers, because a misread and a knowledge gap need completely different remedies.

Classify every wrong answer into one of three causes. A knowledge gap means you did not know the content — the remedy is reading. For adaptive scope. Ordered by value; refined continuously so the top is always ready to pull.

Network and Float Table

Cost baseline = work packages + contingency. Project budget = cost baseline + management reserve.

Every variance is EV minus something. Every index is EV divided by something.

Expected monetary value = probability × impact. Net threats against opportunities.
Compliance Register
Measuring the extent of compliance is a named requirement. Asserted compliance is not compliance.
Closure Checklist
Phase closure and project closure are different. A cancelled project is still closed formally.
Personal Study Plan
Allocate to the gap, not to the domain weighting. Book the date before you leave the room.

fb.t: Every worked example, every workshop and every scenario question in this programme runs on FRIGATE BRAVO. Read this chapter before Day 1 and keep it open all week.

A naval newbuild programme: one lead frigate plus a contracted option for two follow-on hulls. The design is licensed from an international shipbuilding partner. Combat and propulsion systems are imported on long lead and some are export-controlled. The yard delivers under an in-country value (ICV) commitment and under a classification-society survey regime.

How the case develops across the week
•   Day 1 — charter it and govern it: authority, thresholds, tailoring and change control.
•   Day 2 — lead the people: stakeholders across four organizations, the team across three cultures.
•   Day 3 — scope and schedule it: requirements, WBS, backlog, network, critical path.
•   Day 4 — fund and de-risk it: baseline, earned value, contracts, risk register and contingency.
•   Day 5 — control, close and sit the mock: compliance, closure and 180 questions under exam conditions.
